decision_reason: Edgent is a device-edge collaborative DNN inference framework (offline configuration, online tuning, co-inference; Fig. 5 with configurator and runtime optimizer components) prototyped on Raspberry Pi + edge PC, peer-reviewed IEEE TWC 2019 journal article.

extraction.deployment_tech: Not reported (only ML libraries Chainer/BranchyNet named)

evidence.styles: No architectural style named; Sec. IV describes three stages (offline configuration, online tuning, co-inference).
evidence.allocation_strategy: Static: regression latency models + exhaustive search over exit/partition points (Alg. 1); dynamic: configuration map + Bayesian online change point detection selects plan at runtime (Alg. 2-3).
evidence.validation_method: Prototype on Raspberry Pi 3 (device) and desktop PC (edge), branchy AlexNet on CIFAR-10, bandwidth via WonderShaper and 4G/LTE/Oboe traces (Sec. V).

hard_to_decide: IC1: 'IoT' is framed as mobile devices/5G; Raspberry Pi device used, so treated as IoT-class device.
EC5: core contribution is partitioning/early-exit optimisation; included because a framework with named components and device-edge deployment is described, but architecture detail is thin.
training_location: paper says branchy training is 'often done offline on powerful cloud datacenters' but does not state where its own training ran.
Energy explicitly deferred to future work (footnote 1), so not counted as QA.

decision_reason: Abstract describes a generic framework of five architectural alternatives for deploying AI on the edge with edge/cloud (re)training, from an industrial embedded-systems context, in an 8-page SEAA 2020 paper (pp. 21-28); IC3 could not be verified without full text.

quality_attributes: Not reported in abstract (decision factors: data transfer, compute and memory resources)

evidence.styles: Abstract only: 'five architectural alternatives ranging from a centralized architecture where the (re)training is given priority to a decentralized architecture where edge (re)training is given priority'.
evidence.allocation_strategy: Abstract: choice of alternative depends on 'task intent, amount of data needed for (re)training, edge-to-cloud data transfer, available computing and memory resources' (architect's design-time selection).
evidence.validation_method: Abstract: action research in one company + 'qualitative interview study with four additional case companies' (no measured results).

hard_to_decide: Full text not obtainable (IEEE, closed; Semantic Scholar status CLOSED; no repository PDF found) - EC7 flagged, not applied.
IC3: unclear whether alternatives are given as diagrams with components; inclusion is provisional.
IC1: IoT is implied (mobile/IoT data, embedded systems) rather than an explicit IoT system.
validation_method: qualitative interview/action research does not fit the value set; coded as Example scenario.
contribution_type: 'architectural alternatives' sits between design pattern and reference architecture.
Quality scores Q4, Q5, Q9 set low because they cannot be verified from abstract.

decision_reason: Proposes and implements a cloud / edge AIoT micro-cluster / IoT node architecture (Figs. 1-2) deploying containerised microservices and TFLite models on Jetson Nano via Kubernetes, 10-page peer-reviewed MobiSPC 2020 paper in Procedia CS.

evidence.styles: Sec. 3: three levels (cloud servers, edge AIoT micro-cluster, IoT nodes); 'deploy at edge level micro services and adapted artificial intelligence algorithms' in containers orchestrated by Kubernetes.
evidence.allocation_strategy: Sec. 3: placement via pod configuration files / node labels and affinity - microservices on Odroid N2, AI models on Jetson Nano; 'The master node will also be responsible to assign the application to a chosen node depending of its need.'
evidence.validation_method: Sec. 4: Odroid N2 + Jetson Nano cluster vs Tesla P100 cloud; 8+ CNNs on PlantVillage, accuracy and prediction time compared (Table 2).

hard_to_decide: Inconsistencies in text: node counts (4 vs 3 Odroid) and training location (Sec. 3 says Jetson trains, experiments train on cloud P100); coded training as Cloud.
Text claims Jetson is '28 more slow' but Table 2 as extracted shows lower edge times; Q9 given 0.5 because validation covers model accuracy/time only, not architecture latency.
allocation_strategy: Kubernetes scheduler acts at runtime, but placement is fixed by labels/affinity at design time.
Privacy mentioned only as a cloud problem, no mechanism.
